Subject: Follow-up: private connectivity options and next steps

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the Private VPC path vs Dedicated/Hosted choices:

Key takeaways:
- EdgeBank prefers an isolated connectivity model for production workloads (data residency & audit controls).
- You're evaluating Private VPC (PrivateLink or VPC Peering) vs Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Network team needs sample allowlist IPs, port list, and an ops runbook for failover.

Open items (asks from EdgeBank):
1) Which connectivity mode supports your requirements for single-tenant network isolation vs shared endpoint?
2) Sample IP ranges and hostname(s) to allowlist (for both control plane and inference egress).
3) TLS termination model and whether client TLS certs are required.
4) Timeline for a PoC once allowlist/peering details are confirmed.

Next steps I propose:
- Priyom will follow up with a short tech matrix (PrivateLink vs Peering) and a port/IP stub.
- EdgeBank network (please loop in your IT alias) to confirm any firewall/NAT constraints.
- I'll schedule a 30-min network Q&A next week to lock the allowlist and PoC window.

Attachments: postcall-summary.pdf (call notes + proposed PoC outline)

Thanks —
Jordan Blake

Subject: RE: Follow-up: private connectivity options and next steps

Hi Asha —

Thanks — below is a short technical matrix and a minimal allowlist stub you can open for an early PoC. I attached a CSV with common ports plus an XLSX checklist for the full Private VPC onboarding.

PrivateLink (recommended for your case):
- Pros: Managed AWS endpoint (no route table changes in your VPC), predictable DNS CNAMEs, supports fine-grained SG controls.
- Cons: Requires us to provision a VPC endpoint per-region; private DNS override is commonly used.
- TLS: Redwood terminates TLS at the application endpoint. We support mutual TLS for customers on Private (we will share CSR/CA process if required).

VPC Peering:
- Pros: Traffic flows over peered VPCs; lower operational overhead if you manage peering.
- Cons: Cross-account route table complexity, cannot use transitive routing, IP CIDR overlap prevents peering. Peering is best when both sides control CIDR planning.

Minimal PoC allowlist (control plane + inference egress) — open these for a test window:
- Control plane (API endpoints): 52.9.120.34
- Inference egress (short-lived test): 52.9.120.35
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS), 5222 (if webhooks used, confirm firewall) — see attached network-ports-table.csv for full list.

Provisioning notes:
- If you need mutual TLS, we'll provide a CSR template and rotation guidance (we use a 90-day rotation by default).
- For PrivateLink we'll provide vpce IDs and DNS CNAMEs once provisioning starts; those should be added to your internal DNS/allowlist.

Attachments: network-ports-table.csv, redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx

Happy to jump on the network Q&A with your team — propose Thu, Feb 24 at 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Network Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai
